outcomes: In an Nx repository, observe knows which Nx project owns each changed file and which projects depend on it, with or without a graph export
When the CI ran nx graph --file=graph.json, Nx is the authority: its project graph, source imports included, is the one observe uses
Without an export, observe reads the Nx configuration and the package manager workspace, and never runs nx
The change analysis learns where each project's tests write their reports and which lockfile pins its dependencies
nonGoals: Running nx or any package manager command
Edges that only source imports carry, without a graph export: Nx computes them from the code, and the export carries them
Nx plugins that infer projects from files other than project.json and package.json
Mapping changed files and reports to projects, changed-line coverage and lockfile diffs: the change analyses own them
Running the detector as its own extension: it lives in @putnami/observe until a host call runs probes outside a workspace

text: When the repository root holds graph.json, or the file the caller names, and it is an Nx graph export (graph.nodes and graph.dependencies), each project node is a project at its data.root, and each dependency between two project nodes is an edge, whatever its type.
External nodes such as npm packages are dropped.
A missing file is no finding; a file that is not an export is a warning when the caller named it or nx.json exists, and the configuration answers instead.
Without a usable export, a root nx.json makes an Nx workspace.
Its projects are the directories holding a project.json, and those whose package.json the package manager workspace lists; node_modules, dist and hidden directories are skipped.
Edges come from implicitDependencies (names, * patterns, tag: selectors, ! exclusions) and from package dependencies naming another project's package.
A malformed manifest is a warning and is skipped.
Without nx.json and export, there is no Nx project.

Each project's metadata names its Nx project name, the ecosystem nx, its component source (orchestrator for an export, workspace otherwise), the repository-relative outputs of its test targets, and the root lockfile.
A test target is named test, test-*, test:*, *-test or e2e, or its executor ends in :test or runs jest, vitest, playwright or cypress.
Outputs come from the target, else nx.json targetDefaults; Nx tokens are resolved, a glob is cut to its directory, and the rest is dropped.

The detector answers a workspace probe request with a workspace probe result for the extension @putnami/observe: projects keyed by their repository-relative path, the manifest each name was read from, dependencies as project paths, metadata as a JSON object, and the files whose content changes the answer.
The answer passes the probe protocol's strict validation.
A request that names candidate paths gets only the projects among them.
